content: The World Health Organization (WHO) has published several key documents addressing the use of insecticides and pesticides for vector control and public health purposes. Specific documents include: 1. Space Spray Application of Insecticides (2003): This guide provides practical instructions for the use of insecticides in controlling vectors and public health pests through space spraying techniques. 2. Generic Risk Assessment Model for Mosquito Nets (2004): This document outlines a framework for assessing risks associated with the treatment and use of insecticide-treated mosquito nets. 3. Chemical-Specific Adjustment Factors (2005): This guidance focuses on interspecies differences and human variability in dose-response assessments, providing a basis for chemical-specific risk evaluations. 4. Guidelines for Testing Mosquito Larvicides (2005): This publication offers protocols for laboratory and field testing of larvicides used in vector control. 5. 6. Pesticides for Vector Control (2006): The sixth edition of this manual provides comprehensive information on the application of pesticides for controlling vectors and pests of public health importance. 7. 8. Principles for Dose-Response Modelling (2009): This publication outlines principles for modeling dose-response relationships in chemical risk assessments. 9. Risk Assessment of Chemicals in Food (2009): This document provides methods and principles for assessing risks associated with chemicals in food. 10. Field Use of Molluscicides in Schistosomiasis Control (2017): This operational manual is designed for program managers implementing molluscicide use in schistosomiasis control programs. 11. Guidelines for Drinking-Water Quality (2017): The fourth edition, incorporating the first addendum, provides updated recommendations for ensuring safe drinking water. 12. Equipment for Vector Control (2018): This second edition offers specifications and guidelines for equipment used in vector control programs. 13. Generic Risk Assessment Model for Insecticide-Treated Nets (2018): The second edition updates the framework for evaluating risks associated with insecticide-treated mosquito nets. Vector Traps and Risk Assessment Vector traps are devices designed for vector surveillance and control. These traps either capture and kill vectors (capture-kill) or expose them to insecticides or sterilizing agents before release (capture-release). Some traps may use larvicides or adulticides. The human health risk assessment for these traps can be conducted using elements from existing risk assessment models for larviciding and mollusciciding. Environmental risk assessments are generally not proposed due to the minimal pesticide quantities used in traps compared to other vector control methods. Users may be exposed to pesticides while placing them in traps. Trap Servicing: Trap Disposal: Gloves are assumed not to be worn during trap handling due to the manual dexterity required.g. Guidance for assessing inhalation risks can be found in WHO's generic risk assessment models. Other Considerations Product-specific data and local information should be used whenever available to refine risk assessments. Misuse, such as handling traps by children, is not covered in the risk assessment. These guidelines and models provide a comprehensive framework for evaluating the risks associated with various vector control methods, ensuring both efficacy and safety in public health interventions.
